pull.title: fees: prevent divide by zero in CFeeRate
pull.body:
A CFeeRate with size 0 `GetFeePerK()` and `CFeeRate+=` evaluated `EvaluateFeeDown(1000)` unconditionally, dividing by that zero size and crashing.

Return 0 for an empty fee rate, matching `GetFee()` behaviour, and add minimal unit test coverage.

This was reported by Jacob F Cudney (aragondragon)

events.body:
Code review ACK [f442fa2](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36712/changes/f442fa20d437f02518c327736206185bd6f6a1a1)

The fix looks straightforward to me. Checking for an empty rate before the calculation prevents division by zero and matches how `GetFee()` handles it.
Apologies for the comment order, I mistakenly submitted the inline comment first.

comments.body: nit: Could move the tests up to where `GetFee()` returns zero, so that the same tests are grouped? For the next one, could have a newline, as this test is unrelated from the one about "Maximum size in bytes"?

Nit: could we also check the amount returned by `GetFeePerK()` after the addition against the expected amount of 1000?
```suggestion
BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(empty_rate.GetFeePerK(), CAmount{1000});
```
I tried adding this locally and temporarily commenting out `empty_rate += CFeeRate(1, 1)`, leaving the object empty. The existing equality assertion still passed, while this additional check failed with `[0 != 1000]`.
This happens because the comparison uses cross multiplication: `{0, 0}` and `{1, 1}` produce `0 × 1 == 1 × 0`.

With the addition present, both assertions pass. I thought the extra check could help verify the expected result more explicitly and catch a case where the object incorrectly remains empty.
That's a new coverage worth adding, I think. But the goal here is to validate that += does not crash. I believe the current test suffices.
